## Graphic Standards Manual

Week 1. Establish the graphic system used to communicate all later work.

- [Class 01]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-01/) — Week 1 — Aug 25: Begin the Graphic Standards Manual, test a sample sheet and organize your files.

<a id="b02"></a>

## Constructive Solid Geometry

Weeks 2–3. Build editable solids with transformations and Boolean operations.

- [Class 02 · Transformations and Booleans]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-02/) — Week 2 — Sep 1: Move, rotate and scale procedurally. Compare solid Boolean operators and begin the massing study.
- [Class 03 · 3D printing]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-03/) — Week 3 — Sep 8: Refine the CSG process sheet and instructions. Introduce P2b: prepare the CSG object for 3D printing, including units, orientation and slicing.

<a id="b03"></a>

## Descriptive Geometry

Weeks 4–5. Describe geometry through points, lines, edges and faces, then build a parametric solid.

- [Class 04 · Point to solid]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-04/) — Week 4 — Sep 15: Point → Line → Edge → Face → Solid → Boolean. Build the parametric pyramid and reconnect to the CSG project.
- [Class 05 · Your module, material and lighting]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-05/) — Week 5 — Sep 22: Build your own module from points and faces, test its parameter ranges, then render it with one material and a deliberate lighting setup for the P3a sheet.

<a id="b04"></a>

## Arrays 1 — line, grid, cube, curve

Week 6. First of two Arrays classes. Build a row, a grid and a layered array with loops and nested loops, then bend the row onto a curve. Name the count, spacing and index in each direction.

- [Class 06]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-06/) — Week 6 — Sep 29: Submit 2.1 by 11:59 PM. Build a loop and a nested loop — a 1D row, a 2D grid, then 3D layers — then bend the row onto a curve. Name the count, spacing and index in each direction. Check your CSG print file before queueing it.

<a id="b04-second"></a>

## Arrays 2 — if/Switch and math functions

Week 7. Second of two Arrays classes. Patterns begin with a brick wall where every other course shifts; then use if/Switch to select between façade patterns, then shape a cube volume with mathematical functions of X and Y. Hexagonal and radial arrays are optional.

- Class 07 — *not yet released* — Week 7 — Oct 6: Use Compare and Switch to select between façade patterns — a brick wall with every other course shifted is the first example — then shape a cube volume with functions of X and Y. Start from small examples; hexagonal and radial arrays are optional. No graded submission this week (studio reviews).

<a id="b04-support"></a>

## Supported practice — Arrays 1 and 2

Week 8. Supported practice, no new topic. Bring all three array sheets for feedback on repetition, indices, counts and spacing, conditional façade patterns and the mathematical cube volume. Hand in the CSG print.

- Class 08 — *not yet released* — Week 8 — Oct 13: Hand in 2.2 in class, with digital documentation by 11:59 PM. Bring all three array sheets: check the loops, counts and spacing in your 1D/2D/3D arrays, your if/Switch patterns and the mathematical cube volume, and resolve problems before the façade class. No new topic.

<a id="b05"></a>

## Façade attractors — Project 3

Week 9. One façade-attractor class. Combine one curve and one or two point attractors to drive a panel parameter. The next application of attractors is site analysis in Project 4.

- Class 09 — *not yet released* — Week 9 — Oct 20: Submit 3.1. Façade attractors for 3.3: combine one curve and one or two points to drive a panel parameter, then begin the elevation and isometric composition.

<a id="b06"></a>

## Attractor-based site analysis — Project 4

Week 10. Apply attractor measurements to the prepared point cloud using supplied groups. Produce two analytical layers and one design observation for the final project; this is distinct from the façade class.

- Class 10 — *not yet released* — Week 10 — Oct 27: Submit the manual and 3.2. Begin 4.1 with the prepared point cloud and supplied analysis groups: apply attractor measurements to make two analytical layers and one design observation. The class outlines the full Project 4 path, from analysis to a laser-cut model, with brief individual façade feedback.

<a id="b06-volume"></a>

## Generative volume exploration — Project 4

Week 11. Use supplied volume groups to explore three settings of one strategy and select a form for contouring.

- Class 11 — *not yet released* — Week 11 — Nov 3: 4.2 is introduced with supplied volume groups: explore three settings of one generative strategy and select an isometric result. Bring your two site-analysis layers — the check is how they connect to the volume.

<a id="b07"></a>

## Contouring, laser-cut preparation and assembly

Week 12. The last class with new required content, taught through a prepared example with the supplied contouring group: spacing, numbered parts, cutting-file preparation, material/kerf tests, registration, simple assembly and final documentation. 4.3 and 4.4 are introduced here and produced during Weeks 13–15.

- Class 12 · Last new topic — *not yet released* — Week 12 — Nov 10: Bring your selected volume. 4.3 and 4.4 are introduced through a prepared example of the full fabrication workflow: the supplied contouring group, spacing, numbered cutting layouts, material/kerf tests, registration, simple assembly and documentation. You refine your own work in Weeks 13–15. This is the last class with new required content.

<a id="b08"></a>

## Production, feedback and documentation

Weeks 13–15. No new required content. Week 13 checks contours and assembly tests; Week 14 checks fabrication progress and a booklet spread. Week 15 supports production, revisions and final documentation during studio reviews, with no graded submission that day.

- Class 13 · Contours and assembly tests — *not yet released* — Week 13 — Nov 17: Submit 3.3. Bring numbered contours, the cutting layout, an assembly diagram and a small material or registration test. Refine files and begin production with individual feedback. No new topic.
- Class 14 · Laser-cut assembly — *not yet released* — Week 14 — Nov 24: Submit 4.1. Bring tested samples, cutting progress, your assembly and a plan for the remaining work, plus one booklet spread for individual fabrication and presentation feedback. No new topic.
- Class 15 · Connections and final documentation — *not yet released* — Week 15 — Dec 1: No graded submission during studio reviews. Ungraded support for connections, part files, fabrication progress and final documentation.
